Pedralbes — Barcelona, Spain

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Pedralbes is a wealthy, low-density, mostly residential area with no reports found of street crime or violence against pedestrians/tourists. Press coverage instead documents property crime targeting affluent homes and cars (71 home break-ins between Jan 2021-Feb 2022, a Feb 2025 wave of car vandalism/theft). These are property crimes affecting resident homes/vehicles rather than muggings, so night is a cautious yellow rather than red for a visiting traveller on foot. Sources checked: Metropoli Abierta, 2019/2022; Dolça Catalunya, Feb 2025; El Caso/El Nacional.

Frequently asked questions

Is Pedralbes safe?

Wandroz currently rates Pedralbes in Barcelona, Spain as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Pedralbes safe at night?

At night, Pedralbes is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Pedralbes a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Pedralbes's day rating (relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
